title: Memory Leak
description: A 1 KB buffer is appended to a module-level list on every request. RSS grows monotonically. In the early stage there are no latency or error symptoms — the only signal is growing memory.

true_root_cause.summary: memory_leak=true — 1 KB accumulated per request in a module-level list, simulating unbounded cache or response buffer accumulation

key_evidence_signals.expected_behaviour: RSS rises steadily and monotonically; rate ≈ 1 KB × requests/s
Unaffected early on; may rise if GC pressure increases at very high memory

red_herrings: Without the memory panel, the service looks perfectly healthy from latency/error metrics
OOMKill or pod restart (in k8s) would appear as a crash event — not applicable here but worth noting
recommended_fix: Identify and release the unbounded reference (module-level list, cache without TTL, etc.); restart the service to reclaim memory immediately
evaluation_checks: Agent identifies memory_leak as the active flag
Agent cites process_resident_memory_bytes as primary evidence
Agent notes that latency and error rate are stable (rules out other failure modes)
Agent recommends fixing the unbounded reference, not scaling memory
